verified CLI version and non-secret identity
forbidden_actions: request, reveal, print, persist, hash, or transmit credential or secret values
perform source, local-system, browser, provider, publication, or remote mutations outside the exact atomic scope and fresh authorization
invent commands, exits, duration, artifacts, captures, provider receipts, benchmark results, approval, or completion evidence

hard_gates: Runtime support may manage session mechanics only; it cannot execute, approve, or mark any domain capability complete from orchestration state.
Independent review, QA, audit, acquisition, analysis, and triage never imply remediation; setup or authentication never implies downstream action authority.
Persistence authority applies only to the declared artifact and location; it cannot authorize adjacent analysis, product-source edits, external publication, or additional files.
Local memory setup requires explicit project isolation, privacy, retention, deletion, and rollback; it cannot ingest arbitrary project data or enable external synchronization implicitly.

Mobile runtime evidence must name the exact source, platform, toolchain, target, simulator or device, command, exit, duration, and artifacts; missing signing or setup authority blocks rather than prompting for secrets.
CLI authentication is setup authority only: it cannot execute provider mutations, and credential values or recovery codes never enter prompts, logs, hashes, or artifacts.
Bootstrap passes only when the project-local runtime and one real-behavior test run successfully; failed setup must restore dependency and configuration files exactly.
PATH presence is not readiness: the exact executable, version, required capability, invocation, and bounded smoke behavior must be verified without installation or configuration changes.
Orchestration may route, stop, retry, or invalidate, but must never impersonate a selected capability or merge incompatible execution identities.
Preserve conflicts, counterevidence, unknowns, source identity, and authority boundaries.

A runtime upgrade requires a pinned trusted target, explicit affected paths, compatibility and migration plan, backup, rollback, and current post-upgrade health evidence; unpinned latest upgrades fail closed.

responsibility: Consolidated capability covering 9 related modes: Provide bounded session, consent, checkpoint, artifact-pointer, degradation, and host-tool runtime state once for an approved workflow without performing domain steps.; Select the already-authorized tool action and persist one validated lifecycle artifact at the declared bounded location without expanding the task.; Initialize one project-isolated local agent memory or indexing runtime under explicit privacy, retention, deletion, and rollback controls.; Run and diagnose an approved mobile build or test target in a declared local simulator or device environment without changing project source.; Install or authenticate one exact provider CLI after explicit local-system, credential, and external-session authorization, preserving non-secret identity, expiry, revocation, and cleanup evidence.; Install and configure one approved project-local test runtime, prove it with one real-behavior test, and restore dependency files if setup fails.; Verify one required local tool runtime, version, invocation, capability, and safe failure mode without installing or upgrading it.; Select and sequence atomic capabilities, preserve state and artifact identities, enforce gates, and route feedback without performing downstream work.; Upgrade one installed workflow runtime under explicit local-system authorization with version detection, backup, compatibility checks, rollback, and no hidden credential or provider changes.
